newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension funds to take decision on CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension funds to take decision on CVRD.

text.p: A group of seven pension funds will decide today whether or not to sell their minority stake in Brazilian state mining giant CVRD at the company's privatization auction, a pension fund spokeswoman said.
Their decision will determine whether the auction will take place as scheduled April 29, given the CVRD privatization rules.
"The funds are deciding today whether or not they will be selling their shares at the auction," said a spokeswoman for Previ, Brazil's largest pension fund.

The government has to sell-off at least 40 percent of CVRD voting shares at the auction and not more than 45 percent, but the pension funds are in a position to unsettle this arithmetic and turn the auction unviable.
Jointly the seven pension funds hold a 15-percent voting stake in CVRD and as minority shareholders they are allowed to sell their shares alongside the government's at the auction.
Should the pension funds decide to sell their joint 15-percent voting stake at the privatization auction then new sell-off rules and a new auction date would have to be drawn up.
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has introduced incentives for minority shareholders not to sell their CVRD stakes to prevent any possible delay of the auction.
Minority shareholders can exchange their CVRD shares for a stake in state-owned firms Eletrobras or Petrobras rather than sell their shares, a BNDES spokeswoman said.
BNDESpar, the investment arm of BNDES, would exchange the CVRD shares for Eletrobras and Petrobras shares held in its portfolio after the privatization auction, she said.

But, the pension funds have been saying in recent weeks that they are interested in participating in the CVRD auction as buyers rather than sellers, and they have been in talks to join one of the two consortia likely to bid at the auction.
Both steelmaker CSN and metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim, which are leading the two consortia, would like to see the pension funds on their respective teams.
The new owners of the 45-percent CVRD voting block would be in a controling position if they have the pension funds on their side.
